CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's Q1 2026 results were outstanding: revenue up 22% YoY to $17.4B, adjusted EPS of $5.54 beating consensus by ~19%, and a record $63B backlog (+79% YoY). The Power & Energy segment is a secular growth engine driven by AI data center power demand, with plans to nearly triple large reciprocating engine capacity by 2029. Construction Industries revenue surged 38% YoY. However, the stock has already re-rated aggressively — P/E has expanded from ~15.6x a year ago to ~44.3x currently, near the top of its 365-day range (15.6–45.8x). P/B has more than doubled from 8.6x to 22.4x. This extreme valuation expansion prices in much of the good news. Tariff headwinds of $2.2–2.4B for 2026 are compressing margins (operating margin 17.7% vs. prior year), and Resource Industries profit fell 39% due to tariff costs. The balance sheet is solid (equity $18.7B, $4.1B cash) and capital returns are aggressive ($5.7B deployed in Q1 alone). The near-term catalyst — the Q1 earnings beat and raised guidance — has already played out (stock rallied 10% on April 30). The fundamental trajectory is genuinely strong, but the valuation leaves limited margin of safety; the score reflects good fundamentals capped by extreme multiple expansion.
